posts.text:
“Beyond dystopian.”

Novelist Dave Eggers is sounding the alarm about AI, which he argues is harming children’s education: 

“You have a ten-year-old who is unprecedented in the history of the world. There's never been anyone like that person… To think about that one-of-a-kind-in-the-history-of-humanity person shopping their vision out to a machine, how tragic that is. That's beyond dystopian. It cannot be allowed. Not even one ounce of AI can be allowed in the humanities and youth education.”
posts.summary: Highlights concerns about AI's harmful effects on children's education

posts.summary: Defends museum's nonpartisan scholarship against Trump criticism

posts.text: As America turns 250, “it’s really important that we have a commitment to telling the complete story of America,” @smithsonian head Lonnie Bunch tells me. “Our job is to say, how do we tell an accurate history… that challenges America to live up to its ideals?”
posts.summary: Emphasizes need for complete, accurate American historical narratives

posts.text: After 1,000 days of war, the mood in Israel is "somber ... but very much angry," political analyst @dahliasc tells me. Ahead of elections later this year, she tells me why some people are calling Netanyahu's coalition, "the government of the massacre".
posts.summary: Israeli public anger over war toll and Netanyahu's coalition governance

posts.text: Benjamin Netanyahu "needs a war" to stay in power, argues Ami Ayalon, former director of Israeli intelligence service Shin Bet. He tells me why he thinks the Israeli prime minister may be "sacrificing the future of Israel" in his pursuit of eternal war.
posts.summary: Accuses Netanyahu of prolonging war for political survival
